title: Heal stranded .git/index.lock from timeout-killed or crashed git
context: A git operation killed by timeout (TerminateProcess on Windows) or crash leaves .git/index.lock behind. All subsequent git operations fail silently because error paths swallow failures, permanently wedging the sync system—captures report success but nothing commits. Touches invariant(s): con_7217ab24ab (Regression guard: "Flaky test failure under parallelism: native tree-sitter module resolution race on Windows" must not recur.); con_902759b3dc (All JSON writes to .hunch/ must be atomic (temp-file + rename) so an interrupted write can never truncate the index); con_a87360128b (Semantic vectors are a derived layer in SQLite, never the source of truth; reconcile by content hash on reindex).
decision: Add clearStrandedIndexLock() to remove provably-ownerless locks (created by the git we just killed, or older than any live spawn could hold). Integrate into add/commit/merge seams with single retry per attempt. Log removals for observability. Never touch fresh locks.
consequences: Stranded locks heal automatically on next flush, unblocking wedged sync
Single retry after healing avoids unbounded retries without permanent wedging
Windows timeout kills now recover gracefully instead of silently failing
Mtime-based staleness window (30s) is conservative vs actual git timeouts (5–15s), minimizing risk of removing live locks
Adds ~30ms overhead to detect/remove stale locks, negligible vs network I/O
alternatives_rejected: Don't heal; accept permanent wedging, require manual rm .git/index.lock
Always remove any .git/index.lock; simpler but risks orphaning live git operations mid-write
Require explicit recovery call; defeats silent-failure problem since users won't know it's needed
Cooperative locking (PID/timestamp in lock file); invasive changes to git integration layer
